notes: The catalogue names Chatrasiṃha as scribe, but the name does not appear in the quoted colophon. The colophon has two dates. The verse date reads 'āṣāḍhakṛṣṇapakṣe caturarāsigate raviravaśuravigate samvat'. It is garbled: perhaps a corrupt chronogram, perhaps a weekday such as ravivāra, but it cannot be read. The prose date reads NS 883 jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa 13 (trayodaśī), followed by 'āṣāḍhasya'. The two month names do not conflict: kṛṣṇapakṣa āṣāḍha in the pūrṇimānta reckoning is the same fortnight as jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa in the amānta reckoning. NS 883 = c. 1763 CE (May–June). The verse is a genealogy of the Upamanyu lineage: Bhavānīdāsa; his son Priyaṃvada ('priyaṃvada' could also be an epithet, 'sweet-speaking', of an unnamed son); in that family the elder Vīrabhadra, then Hari(-)śaṅkara (one person or two); a brother whose name begins with Śiva ('tattrātā śivapūrvvanāma' = tadbhrātā); and his unnamed son ('tatsunu ... satsaṃpradāyakaviḥ'). That unnamed son is probably the scribe or the person behind this copy. The final Newari line ('vidyānaṃ dayā kabho cā bhāju nasya ṅā juroḥ') is corrupt. 'Vidyānandayā' looks like a genitive. 'nasya ṅā juro' might be nyāṅā julo ('was bought'), which would make this a sale or ownership note, but that is uncertain. Kabhocā could also be a place or a misreading. The roles of Vidyānanda and Kabhocā are therefore left as 'other'.
